scope: Named foreign shareholders (≥1%) of five NIFTY 50 constituents assigned as batch 3 — Coal India Limited, Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Limited, Eicher Motors Limited, Eternal Limited (formerly Zomato) and Grasim Industries Limited — from primary SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b) quarterly shareholding-pattern filings opened directly where reachable within budget. Eicher Motors (quarter ended 31.03.2026, via eicher.in's own BSE-XBRL render) and Grasim Industries (quarter ended 30.06.2026, via grasim.com's own PDF) were opened as full primary filings. Eternal Limited was opened via a Zomato/Eternal-hosted PDF (b.zmtcdn.com) but only a September 2025 quarter (30.09.2025) was locatable within budget — noted as possibly superseded by a more recent quarter not checked. Coal India and Dr. Reddy's Laboratories could not be opened as primary filings within budget: coalindia.in returned 403 on every route tried (current investor pages) and only stale pre-2019 archive.coalindia.in PDFs surfaced by search; drreddys.com returned 404 on both a search-indexed PDF path and a guessed investor-relations path, and the company's SEC Form 20-F (which would carry a 'Major Shareholders' item) exceeded the fetch tool's size limit. Both are recorded at screener.in aggregate, tier reported, per the domain's fallback instruction, with the primary-source attempts logged as voids. This file also surfaces two Temasek Holdings (Singapore) subsidiary vehicles (Dunearn Investments (Mauritius) Pte Ltd, Camas Investments Pte Ltd) holding a combined 2.87% of Eternal — outside SPEC's mandatory comparison set (Temasek is institutionally distinct from GIC, the comparison-set Singapore holder: GIC manages Singapore's foreign reserves, Temasek is the state's investment-holding company) but material and recorded for accuracy. It confirms one comparison-set holder, Capital Group (via its 'New World Fund Inc' vehicle, 1.35% of Eicher Motors), and Norges Bank/NBIM (via 'Government Pension Fund Global', 1.12% of Eternal) as directly named ≥1% holders — the first sightings of either in this research pass across both this batch and the batch-1 file's five companies. BlackRock, Vanguard, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority and ADIA were not found as named ≥1% holders in any of the three companies where a primary filing was opened.

symmetryCheck: The same lens applied to this batch's five companies found LIC (the domestic control) named ≥1% and quantified in 2 of 3 companies actually opened at primary-source granularity — Eicher Motors (1.14%) and Grasim Industries (6.59%, the largest single named institutional shareholder in that company after the Birla promoter group) — and unnamed/below-threshold in the third (Eternal). This mirrors the companion holders.json file's finding: LIC clears 1% more often and by a wider margin than any single mandatory-comparison-set foreign holder. Of the mandatory comparison set, only two names surfaced anywhere in this batch: Capital Group (1.35% of Eicher Motors, via New World Fund Inc) and NBIM/Norges Bank (1.12% of Eternal, via Government Pension Fund Global) — both single sightings, both in the 1.0–1.4% range, neither approaching a control stake. BlackRock, Vanguard, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority and ADIA were absent by name from every company where a primary filing was opened in this batch, consistent with the companion file's finding that passive-index and diversified-mandate holders rarely cross the 1% per-vehicle naming threshold in any single Indian company even when the underlying manager's aggregate India AUM is large. The batch's most concentrated non-domestic holder by far was not in the comparison set at all: Temasek Holdings, at a combined 2.87% of Eternal across two vehicles — larger than any comparison-set holder found in any of the eight companies opened across this file and its companion (holders.json) to date. Run on the two foreign promoter-linked holders found here — Suzuki Motor Corporation in the companion file's Maruti Suzuki sample, and P.T. Indo Bharat Rayon (part of the Birla family's own overseas promoter-group structure) in this batch's Grasim sample — the lens shows the same pattern twice: a single foreign-registered promoter/promoter-group vehicle dwarfs every passive FPI line in its own company, and in neither case is that vehicle a passive index fund of the kind the 'BlackRock owns India' narrative is about.
